chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Make this matter of yours for the sake of Allah, and do not make it for the people, for whatever is for Allah is for Allah, and whatever is for the people, it does not ascend to the sky.'
And do not dispute with the people regarding your Religion, for disputing is a sickness of the heart.
Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah Guides whom He Desires.
Will you then force the people until they become Believers?

Leave off the people, for the people are taking (their Religion) from the people, and you all are taking from Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and Ali (peace be upon him), and there is no equation.
And indeed I heard my father saying: 'When Allah Ordains for a servant to enter into this matter (Al-Wilayah), he would be quicker to it than the bird to its nest'.

key_terms.لِلنَّاسِ: For the people / For public display
key_terms.لِلَّهِ: For the sake of Allah / Dedicated to Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of dedicating religious matters to Allah alone and avoiding disputes with people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises believers to dedicate their religious affairs solely to Allah rather than for public display, warning that disputes over religion corrupt the heart. He cites Quranic verses to illustrate that guidance is Allah's domain, not forced by humans, and emphasizes that the Ahl al-Bayt's authority is distinct from the people's derived knowledge. This narration underscores the Shia principle of *al-Tabligh* (conveyance) without compulsion (*Ikrah*), highlighting that the Imams' role is to transmit the divine message faithfully, leaving the actual acceptance of faith to Allah's will.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from his father who said, 
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Make this matter of yours for the sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and do not make it to be for the people for whatever was for the sake of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so it is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and whatever was for the people, so it would not ascend to the sky; and do not dispute with the people with your Religion, for the disputing is a sickness of the heart.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said to Hisazwj Prophetsaww [28:56] Surely you cannot guide whom you love, but Allah Guides whom He Desires to, and He is more Knowing of the recepients of Guidance.

And Heazwj Said [10:99] will you then force the people until they become Believers? Leave off the people, for the people are taking (their Religion) from the people, and you all are taking from Rasool-Allahsaww and Aliasws, and there is no equation, and Iasws heard myasws fatherasws saying: ‘When Allahazwj Ordains for a servant to enter into this matter (Al-Wilayah)), he would be quicker to it than the bird it’s to its nest’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from his father who has said the following:
“Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘Keep your cause (belief), for the sake of Allah and do not make it for people; what is for Allah is for Allah and what is for people cannot ascend to heaven.
Do not argue with people about your religion; argumentation causes sickness to the heart.
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said to His Holy Prophet, ‘(Muhammad), you cannot guide whomever you love, but Allah guides whomever He wants. . . .’ [28:56]
He has also said, ‘. . . (Muhammad), do you force people to have faith’? [10:99].

Leave the people alone; they take it from people and you take it from the Messenger of Allah and from Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali ibn abu Talib), recipients of divine supreme covenant, and this is not equal.
I heard my father saying, ‘When Allah writes for a servant to enter into this cause (belief of AM al-Bayt) he rushes to it quicker than a bird to its nest.’”
